title: Short Stuff: The Death of Billy the Kid
summary: Short Stuff episode on the death of Billy the Kid. The hosts open by joking about the Billy Joel song "The Ballad of Billy the Kid," the Young Guns and Pat Garrett and Billy the Kid films, and a Billy Joel piano video. They then cover Billy's background (born William Henry McCarty Jr., also known as William Bonney, orphaned at fourteen, a Lincoln County regulator), the Lincoln County War that followed the killing of Tunstall, and his capture by Pat Garrett's posse at Stinking Springs. While awaiting execution in the Lincoln County Courthouse he killed deputy James Bell during an escape attempt and then shot John Olinger. The hosts then describe Garrett's ambush-style reputation, the July 1881 killing at Peter Maxwell's house in Fort Sumner (the account of Billy going for meat, the disputed ambush version involving Maxwell, and Billy's real age), the persistent rumors that he survived, and the coda that William Koch bought the original tintype for $2.3 million and that Garrett finally received the reward.

segments.title: Billy the Kid's background
segments.summary: Billy was born William Henry McCarty Jr. in New York, went by William Bonney, was orphaned at fourteen, and became one of the Lincoln County regulators hired for a man named Tunstall, whose killing set off the Lincoln County War.

segments.title: Capture and jailbreak
segments.summary: Pat Garrett's posse captured Billy at Stinking Springs and he was held in a locked room at the Lincoln County Courthouse. He shackled-escaped by killing deputy James Bell, then shot Bob Olinger when Olinger came looking for him, and fled town.

segments.title: Pat Garrett's pursuit and the Fort Sumner killing
segments.summary: Garrett tracked Billy down about four months later in July 1881 at Peter Maxwell's house near Fort Sumner, where Billy was reportedly involved with Maxwell's sister. Garrett's official account says Billy walked in with a knife and gun looking for meat and was shot in the dark. Hosts say the truth was likely an ambush, with Billy probably unarmed, and that Maxwell may have set him up. Rumors that Billy survived are dismissed as unsupported, with exhumations and DNA tests inconclusive.

segments.title: Coda: tintype sale and reward
segments.summary: Billy's famous tintype photo original plate was bought for $2.3 million by William Koch. Garrett was first denied the $500 reward, then after city residents raised money and a later vote, he received it, worth roughly two hundred thousand dollars today. Hosts close the episode.
